```markdown
### Source Issue #660: Route-weights export published source_version 0 (empty Brain) and overwrote an evidenced publication; bind the DB path and refuse evidence regressions
Keepalive: OFF
Base: main
Head: codex/issue-660

Source: https://github.com/stranske/Orchestrator/issues/660

> ## Why
> 
> The route-weights export published to `exports/route-weights/config/route-weights.json` at 2026-10-17T03:53:44Z carries `source_version: 0` and `evidence_ok: false` with `ranking: []` for every task type, while the live Brain at `~/.codex/orchestrator/feedback/orchestrator.db` is at weight version 68 with `implement` observations codex 1198, cursor 445, gemini 101, vibe 137, claude 450 (read-only check, 2026-10-17 04:30Z). Rebuilding the export from the live DB yields `implement` ranking length 4. The publisher therefore ran against an empty or wrong database and replaced an evidenced publication with an evidence-less one; the change detector accepted it because the content differed. Every consumer of the export (stranske/Workflows `agent_delegation_policy.js`, the intake chooser from Workflows#3991) now falls back to its static default, so the learned routing that Priority 3 depends on is silently off. Nothing reported it: `route_weights_export.py` neither binds the DB path explicitly nor refuses to publish a regression from evidenced to evidence-less content.
> 
> Campaign concept (value-chain gate): situation = every daily export publish; demand = one publish per day plus every capacity-state change; pass number = the published export has `source_version > 0` and `task_types.implement.ranking` length ≥ 2 on every check, and the exporter's log shows one refused publish when fed an empty DB in the test; printed by `gh api repos/stranske/Orchestrator/contents/config/route-weights.json?ref=exports/route-weights` and the exporter's test. Check date: next daily export after merge, then the weekly check 2026-10-20.
> 
> ## Scope
> 
> - `src/route_weights_export.py`: resolve the feedback DB path explicitly (the same resolver `feedback.py` uses, with `ORCH_STATE_DIR` honoured) and log the resolved path and `source_version` on every run
> - a publish guard: refuse to publish when `source_version == 0`, when every task type has `evidence_ok: false`, or when the new document would set `evidence_ok` false for a task type the currently published document has true, unless `--allow-evidence-regression` is passed; print the refusal reason
> - tests for the path binding and the three refusal conditions
> - `orchestrate.sh` cadence step: surface the refusal in the tick log
> 
> ## Non-Goals
> 
> - Do not change thresholds (`n_obs >= 20`), the 120-day window or the exclusion classes
> - Do not change the v1 schema or the capacity block
> - A guard that only logs and still publishes is not completion
> 
> ## Tasks
> 
> - [ ] In `src/route_weights_export.py`, replace the implicit DB lookup with the shared resolver from `feedback.py` and log `db=<path> source_version=<n>` at the start of every run.
> - [ ] Add `publish_guard(new_doc, published_doc) -> (ok, reason)` implementing the three refusal conditions; call it before any publish; exit non-zero with the reason when refused.
> - [ ] Add `--allow-evidence-regression` for a deliberate owner-approved downgrade, logged.
> - [ ] Add tests in `tests/test_route_weights_export.py`: empty DB → refused; all-false evidence → refused; published true → new false → refused; flag → allowed; path resolver honours `ORCH_STATE_DIR`.
> - [ ] Update the export README and the ARCHITECTURE.md export paragraph with the guard.
> - [ ] After merge and mirror sync, run one publish from the live DB and record `source_version` and `implement` ranking length in the PR.
> 
> ## Acceptance Criteria
> 
> - [ ] `pytest tests/test_route_weights_export.py` passes.
> - [ ] Deliberate-break gate: temporarily make `publish_guard` return `(True, "")` unconditionally; the empty-DB test fails naming the guard; revert and rerun green. Capture both outcomes in the PR body.
> - [ ] `python3 src/verify.py` passes.
> - [ ] The next published export has `source_version > 0` and `task_types.implement.ranking` length ≥ 2.
> 
> ## Implementation Notes
> 
> - `src/route_weights_export.py:57-96, 226-234` (version read, retention rule, evidence flag)
> - `src/feedback.py:271-294` (window and eligibility), DB resolver
> - Orchestrator CLAUDE.md §2 "Learning-loop integrity": a publication that drops evidence is a Brain-integrity event and belongs in that section's rules
> - Capability Program tracker stranske/Orchestrator#575, routing unit
> 
```

### ⚠️ Capability Check: Some tasks may need human assistance

**Recommendation:** REVIEW_NEEDED

**✅ Actionable Tasks (7):**
- In src/route_weights_export.py, replace the implicit DB lookup with the shared resolver from feedback.py and log db=<path> source_version=<n> at the start of every run.
- Add publish_guard(new_doc, published_doc) -> (ok, reason) for the three specified refusal cases, invoke it before publishing, and exit non-zero with the refusal reason.
- Add --allow-evidence-regression for the explicit owner-approved evidence-regression override and log its use.
- Add tests in tests/test_route_weights_export.py for empty DB refusal, all-false evidence refusal, true-to-false published-evidence refusal, override-flag allowance, and ORCH_STATE_DIR resolver behavior.
- Update the export README and ARCHITECTURE.md export paragraph to document the publish guard.
- Run pytest tests/test_route_weights_export.py and fix implementation/test failures under agent control until it passes.
- Run python3 src/verify.py and fix implementation/verification failures under agent control until it passes.

**⚠️ Partial Tasks (2):**
- Deliberate-break gate: temporarily make publish_guard return (True, "") unconditionally; confirm the empty-DB test fails naming the guard; revert and rerun green; capture both outcomes in the PR body.
  - *Limitation:* The agent can perform the temporary local change, run both test states, revert it, and prepare the exact PR-body text. It cannot update or guarantee updating a hosted PR body without external-service credentials.
- After merge and mirror sync, run one publish from the live DB and record source_version and implement ranking length in the PR.
  - *Limitation:* The agent can prepare or run the publish command only where the live DB and publish access are available. Merge, mirror synchronization, access to live state, publishing to external destinations, and PR updates may require human credentials and post-merge operational access.

**🚫 Blocked Tasks (1):**
- Acceptance criterion: the next published export has source_version > 0 and task_types.implement.ranking length >= 2.
  - *Reason:* This depends on the contents and availability of the live DB, an actual post-merge publish, and potentially authenticated external publishing infrastructure. The agent cannot guarantee that the next production export contains the required live data or perform credentialed external operations.
  - *Suggested Action:* After merge and mirror sync, a human with live-state and publishing access should run the export, verify source_version is greater than zero and the implement ranking has at least two entries, then record the observed values in the PR.

**👤 Human Actions Needed:**
- Confirm the exact intended semantics of the three refusal conditions if they are not already established by existing export/document schemas and tests.
- Provide owner approval before using --allow-evidence-regression for a real downgrade.
- Merge the change and ensure mirror synchronization completes.
- Run the post-merge publish against the live DB using authorized access.
- Verify the published export has source_version > 0 and task_types.implement.ranking length >= 2.
- Add the deliberate-break test results and the live-publish source_version/ranking-length evidence to the hosted PR body.

Finding for the implementer: the 03:53:46Z publication was committed as `orchestrator-export`, not by the local tick (whose log shows `unchanged` at that time and whose commits are authored by the owner). The exporter's fallback git identity signs when it runs outside the owner's environment. The likely publisher is an agent run executing the post-merge task 'run the export once with ORCH_ROUTE_WEIGHTS_PUBLISH=1' from an isolated agent runtime where `~/.codex/orchestrator/feedback/orchestrator.db` does not exist, so the Brain read as version 0. The guard must therefore (a) refuse to publish when the resolved DB is missing or has version 0, regardless of who runs it, and (b) log the resolved DB path and identity in the publish commit message. Remediation already applied: republished version 68 from the live Brain at 04:02:41Z.
